Consider the d’Alembert differential equation

y=x(1+dydx)+(dydx)2.

If y′(x)=t, then general solution can be expressed in parametric form (x(t),y(t)), where

x(t)=Ce−t+f(t) and C is an arbitrary constant. Find the function f(t).

Hint: Under the given transformation, we have dxdt+x=−2t. You may also wish to make use of the following result (constants omitted): ∫tetdt=(t−1)et
